WHEN PLAYING MEETS EARNING: THE PLAY TO EARN GAME MODEL ON BLOCKCHAIN TECHNOLOGY

[Banner: Gaming, the elephant in the room]

Tracing the Roots of Game Evolution

From the times when arcade machines were a rad trend to the boom of console wars along with crazy PC mods packing extreme power under the HUD to times when professional gaming and its market has made its common place even on our mobile phones. Gaming has been an industry, ever evolving into different directions and expanding the horizons. With big tech giants investing and catering to gaming as a media, working solely to bring innovation at an ever progressing rate.

Gaming is no longer that simple childhood fever for boys that parents used to shrug about. It has in fact become a million-dollar market. In 2018, Reuters announced that gaming had surpassed other entertainment media such as movies, TVs, and music in terms of revenue, and this meteoric rise is showing no signs of slowing down. From children to adults, boys to girls, entrepreneurs to corporations, everyone has some sort of part in it and if not, they certainly want one.

One particular thing to be noted here is how the gaming industry has evolved in its nature to pitch the products to the consumers. From times when player vs player was a popular concept on arcades and leaderboards, gaming took a shift with introduction to dynamic storytelling and campaign oriented niches. This further evolved into full scale exploration projects with vast open worlds waiting to be discovered. Every game developer had ideas and everyone wanted to do something exquisite morphing the industry to be a plethora of creativity.

The Free to Play Games That Are Not So Free

With every step of evolution and money invested in gaming projects, the value of the market increased with full scale corporate competitions on the line. Having said, obviously things took to a level where gaming became quite an expensive hobby. From console prices to buying each sort of physical copy of games with extra added content to be bought digitally and to be paid extra for.

But here is the thing, the money you invested on gaming could somehow still give you a return value. After all, it was physical assets you held in your hand. You could sale your console and games even making profits if you had special editions which are considered rare and sought by the collectors. But, everyone does not want to join the gaming frenzy with its full hype. Many would like to enjoy but at their own pace and for that, they would not be willing to spend hundreds of dollars. And so, comes into the market a new model of games, focused more on PC and mobile platforms, the Free to Play games. Obviously a thought comes to mind, hey, the developers spend years and tons of cash to develop launch and market the game and I am playing it for free. What’s in it for them?

To answer them, a bit of psychology comes into play. These special games are marketed and crafted in a certain manner. Humans have a compulsive nature by default. Using the same principles that casinos deploy to keep the players gambling, these games do the same with time and effort being the investment instead of money, but, it does not stop there. The key goal is to still get the money out of your pockets into theirs. After hooking you to the game and making it as immersive as possible, with every day logins and better rewards to play more and more, the game is designed to make you want to be better and get the most out of it. And to be better, you have to pay a price. That is where the pay to win model comes into play.

Invest your cash in the game on different collectibles, items and skins in an attempt to stand out and feel special and curate a personality to define you inside the game. These items at times do give you an edge over the other players be it a psychological aspect of it or a technical one. The game is equipped with mechanisms of gambling. Unlike buying and paying for something you like directly, the game makes you spend money on things like loot boxes or lucky spins to try your luck and pay more than just once for the items that you require, making you pay again and again until you get the thing that you desired, only for them to launch something even better in the next update that you now, again, want as well.

Similarly, offering special skins for your avatars or even giving you special characters that can only be bought, the game indirectly forces you to pay to them for enjoying the game. And once the first step has been taken, return is not easy because if you leave the game, all your time, money and hard work is boom, lost. But like the ever changing game market, evolution is on its way with a newer system and technology.

[Banner: Combining the art of playing and Earning]

The Player Who Plays to Earn

A very common imagination for gamers is, ‘ahh, if gaming was a job and we were paid to play.’ While many have realized this dream by becoming influencers and content creators, and others joining the industry to take their slice of the cake, the fact remains that in this world where more than half of the world’s population has partook in gaming one way or another, there are millions who still think of the fantasy to earn with gaming.

If a person were to come to tell you, a couple of years earlier that he will pay you to play for no added benefit, that would clearly have been super suspicious, but, I take it upon myself to be the bearer of news that it is certainly possible. Perhaps not in the elusive manner of thought that you may have imagined but still very much possible with potential and roots to grow for more. The reason for this is the developing rise of the of WEB3 and blockchain systems. While not going into details on those themes for now, Play to earn is a byproduct of a concept that aims at decentralization.

Decentralization basically aims to create a trend where the economy and finance power instead of staying in the hands of the top brass, the game developers and publishers in our example, lays equally in the hands of the consumer as well. The concept of DE financing this in the gaming realm is part of the topic of Gamefi which blockchain and WEB3 focuses on. It aims to give the power to the player and own what he invests, basically DE financing the gaming monopoly.

The practicality of what was once a dream

Games build on the blockchain model enable players to convert the in game assets into something they own and control basically giving the power to change the value of such assets into the hands of the players. Think of a game. Let’s say Saints Row. You start with zero, build up a whole empire and then end the game. In the end, the only thing you are taking away with you are the fond memories of a wonderful experience. While that’s not a bad deal, imagine if I tell you that all the money you earned inside game could somewhat become tangible for you to utilize in a way that it becomes a financial asset helping you in the real world as well.

While it may not be possible for high end campaign oriented games like Saints Row for now, this is a start of a new generation of gaming model which will only keep on increasing with the rise of investments with big tech giant and corporates into systems like metaverse and blockchain.

For now, the games on blockchain that, in their development model may still be somewhat centralized, but still having the potential to give rise to what may be called an ‘open in-game economy.’ More on that in a while. Games can become play to earn, with player-driven value accrual allowing for the birth of robust, unique, and formal economies using NFT’s or crypto, connecting the in game items to the actual real world market.

Here is a simple explanation. You earn and build some asset in the game. You can then take those assets and sell, lease or exchange them on an open market. This cross platform interaction is possible because everything you earn in these games is linked to you with tokens verifying your ownership over the items. Hence why, you do not need the permission of the game creators to trade and are free to do so as you like. A very similar idea to explain this would be the concept of trading card games. Like Pokémon for example. You bought the cards once which benfitted the creators, but you owned them afterwards, enabling you to freely trade or sell with other card players at your own accord giving rise to a system and trend that increased the value of these cards and benefitting both the players and creators. This way, even if you stop playing a game, all your assets can be sold and exchanged into other usable assets retaining the value of your investments.

The developers of the game benefit with you dealing in with their tokens or currencies. The more a token is used in the market, the higher its value rises benefiting both the players and the developers. This way players get the power to actively change the trends in the gaming market with their own hands and choices. This gives rise to what is called an open in game economy.

Closed Economies and Open Marketplaces

The traditional gaming examples are models working on the principles of closed market game economies. In such a system, the initial price of an in game item is set without a change in value which is lost once the item has been bought. This puts a cap on the growth of in-game value from a free-market perspective. Items are statically priced, and in-game value never has a chance to grow. No matter how rare or valuable the item, players have no means to build upon the initial item release and create hierarchies of items with increasing values that ultimately benefit both players and the game developer.

The centralized companies who control the video game business nowadays have the power to take away a player's ownership of an item or to outright decide to prohibit in-game item exchanges, keeping the initial in-game value for themselves and eliminating the possibility of player-generated growth. Even though players create the majority of the value in online multiplayer games, they have little say over how much in-game money or products are worth.

This is the point at which NFTs and cryptocurrency become vital for enhancing player control and creating an even playing field for all parties involved in video games. Sovereign item ownership games put more emphasis on promoting collective player autonomy through permissionless marketplaces and verifiable ownership of digital assets than on a player's ability to make money from gaming, thus unleashing the full potential of in-game value.

Blockchains and NFTs, which are based on transparency, decentralisation, and group decision-making, can serve as a fundamental basis upon which new games can be developed with these principles in mind, or they can assist established games in their transition to a more equitable and fair system, thereby creating the possibility of truly player-owned games.
